columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Thinkific Labs Inc. cloud-based course creation and delivery.
2024 revenue: USD 60M ARR (up from USD 34.7M in 2021); some reports estimate ≈USD 70.9M annual revenue and ~399 employees.
29.7K customers using Thinkific to run courses and learning businesses.
Creators on Thinkific have reportedly generated USD 3.7B+ in sales by 2026.

strengths.title: Strong course platform for professionals
strengths.detail: Solid course builder, hosting, and delivery, well suited to professional and B2B courses.

strengths.title: Generous course publishing
strengths.detail: Unlimited published courses on all plans from day one.

strengths.title: No extra platform fees via Thinkific Payments
strengths.detail: With Thinkific Payments, creators typically pay ~2.9% processing with no extra platform transaction charges.

strengths.title: User-friendly course builder
strengths.detail: Course creation is genuinely approachable with no technical skills required.

weaknesses.title: Higher entry price and no free tier
weaknesses.detail: Basic plan starts around USD 49/month and lacks some core features; no long-term free plan.

weaknesses.title: Feature gating at higher tiers
weaknesses.detail: PayPal at checkout, removing Thinkific branding, API/webhooks, and advanced analytics often require the ~USD 199/month Grow plan.

weaknesses.title: Limited analytics at lower tiers
weaknesses.detail: Little analytics improvement from Basic to Start despite a price jump; advanced engagement analytics sit at higher tiers.

weaknesses.title: No built-in student support tools
weaknesses.detail: Reviews note a lack of built-in student support and coaching features at lower tiers.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Thinkific is course hosting, student accounts, and checkout for teachers running their own course brand. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Thinkific is a learning commerce platform.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Thinkific side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Thinkific you can use Courses, Memberships, Community & Messaging, and Storefronts as first-class product jobs. You are running a full course engine: drip, quizzes, student progress, and checkout that already works.

Using Kahana with Thinkific

You can use both. Thinkific keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep the course engine on Thinkific for drip, quizzes, and enrollment. Also list or link that teaching on Kahana so Explore, Clubs, and Aura can give it another place to be found. Thinkific stays the LMS; Kahana is another surface for exposure.
